title: Supply, demand and inventory reports

inOneLine.simple: When more is produced than used, stored amounts rise. When less is produced than used, they fall. An [[inventory-report|inventory report]] shows which is happening.
inOneLine.balanced: Inventory change ≈ supply − demand over the period. A draw (fall) bigger than expected can suggest tighter supply; a surprise build the opposite. As with any release, the [[surprise]] against the [[consensus-forecast|consensus]] matters more than the headline, and the reaction is never certain.

explain.simple: Think of a giant tank. Production and imports pour in; factories, refineries and buyers take out. If more goes in than comes out, the level rises: that is a build. If more comes out, the level falls: that is a draw. Many commodities have regular reports on stored amounts. Before each report, forecasters publish what they expect. Prices often react to the gap between the actual change and the expected change, not to the change itself. All countries, reports and figures here are fictional.
explain.balanced: Supply comes from production, imports and stored stock; demand from use and exports. Production can take months or years to change, so short-term moves are often about stocks in storage. Reports have several parts, such as crude, fuel products and regional figures, and they can disagree. Traders may also have expected something different from the published consensus. So a big draw might lift prices, do nothing, or even be followed by a fall if it was already priced in. Treat each report as a scenario with several possible outcomes.

assumptions: Fictional country: Northland. Fictional weekly report on crude oil in storage
Supply into storage this week: 10.0 million barrels; taken out: 11.5 million
Consensus forecast: a draw of 0.5 million barrels
steps: Inventory change = 10.0 − 11.5 = −1.5 million barrels, a draw.
The draw was 1.0 million barrels bigger than expected, which hints at tighter supply.
Scenario thinking: price might rise, rise then fade, or barely move. Do not pick one as certain.

assumptions: Same fictional Northland report, a different week
Consensus: a draw of 0.5 million barrels
Actual: a build of 0.8 million barrels
steps: More is in storage than expected, which hints at looser supply or weaker use.
Story 1: prices fall as traders see more supply than they thought.
Story 2: fuel stocks drew sharply in the same report, and that detail dominates. Prices hardly move.
Same headline surprise, different outcomes, depending on the details and on what was priced in.

explainSimpler: Watch the tank level and compare it with what people guessed. A bigger fall than guessed can mean tight supply, but the market may already have guessed right.
commonMistake: Reading a draw as 'bad' because a number fell. A draw means more was used than added, which points to tighter supply, not weaker demand. And the sign of the surprise matters more than the sign of the change.

quickCheck.prompt: Fictional report: consensus a build of 1.0 million barrels, actual a draw of 2.0 million. What is the surprise?

options.explanation: No: actual minus consensus is −2.0 − (+1.0), which is negative.
No: that adds the two numbers instead of subtracting.
Right: −2.0 − (+1.0) = −3.0 million barrels, a much tighter week than expected.

quickCheck.prompt: Stored amounts of a commodity fall more than expected. What is the most accurate reading?

options.text: Supply is likely tighter than thought, but the price reaction is not certain
options.explanation: Right: a tendency only. It may have been priced in, or other details may dominate.

options.text: Demand is weak, so the price will certainly fall this week
options.explanation: No: a draw means use exceeded supply, and no reaction is certain.

options.text: Supply may be looser than thought, so prices may slip
options.explanation: No: a bigger draw than expected points to tighter supply, not looser.

quickCheck.prompt: In one week, 8.0 units go into storage and 6.5 units come out. What happened?

options.explanation: No: more went in than came out, so the level rose.
